about: The no-drop half of the job, on Kunal's 'Keep today's letter colours' (questions/B9C-COORD-CONTRAST, 10 Nov 2026; DECISIONS-LOG.md): every board letter reads its theme's light/dark pair on an opaque chip, highlighted or not, and is painted above the highlight - on a puzzle's Show square (e1) and on a flipped board with g8 selected, at 375x761 with his insets and 320x568. Graded by gate 207 (TC-R326..327), reading each label's own computed ink and chip. NOT COVERED: raising the pair to WCAG AA 4.5:1 (his answer is keep); themes other than the default (their pairs are what the opaque chip paints).

breaks.name: the-letters-lose-their-chip
breaks.why: the #548 chip is stripped, so the highlight under a letter is what it is read against again (the 1.58:1 case)

breaks.name: the-letters-sit-under-the-highlight
breaks.why: the letters drop below the highlight layer, so the overlay paints over them

breaks.name: the-file-letters-take-a-faint-ink
breaks.why: the file letters take a faint translucent ink instead of the other square's colour, under their own pair
